messages.content: I have the three lodging options open now. Can you run the full six-night numbers for May 20 through May 26 and check the details that could actually change the decision? The hotel portion needs to stay at or below $2,250 before any separate parking.

Yes. Send me the displayed room rate, taxes or fees, parking terms, and room type for each one. I’ll separate the hotel total from parking so the $2,250 limit stays clear, then compare shoreline access and cancellation language.

Option one is Cypress Cove Inn in Pacific Grove. Standard king, $315 a night. The checkout screen shows 12% tax and a $12 local assessment for the stay. Parking says complimentary. It also says eight minutes to the shoreline, but I want to know whether that means an actual walk or marketing language.

For six nights, the room subtotal is $1,890. Tax is $226.80, and the assessment is $12, making the hotel total $2,128.80. Parking adds $0, so the complete six-night cost remains $2,128.80. That leaves $121.20 under the hotel limit.
What can you confirm about the walk and the room? I remember this being the smaller room.

The property page places the inn about 0.4 mile from the nearest public shoreline access near Asilomar, and its walking directions estimate eight to nine minutes on neighborhood streets. It is not beachfront, and the route does not appear to require driving. The standard king listing is 235 square feet with one king bed, a mini refrigerator, and a coffee maker. It does not promise an ocean view or balcony. Complimentary on-site parking is included for one vehicle.

Good. Option two is Harbor Street Hotel in Monterey. It is $270 nightly, same 12% tax and $12 assessment. Parking is $28 a night. The room is a deluxe king. The attraction is being able to walk to dinner.

Its six-night room subtotal is $1,620. Tax is $194.40 and the assessment is $12, so the hotel portion is $1,826.40. Six nights of parking adds $168, bringing the complete stay to $1,994.40. It is $134.40 less than Cypress Cove after parking and leaves $423.60 under the hotel limit before parking.
Does it really put us near restaurants, and what does the room include? Also check the coast claim carefully.

The map supports the restaurant advantage: several places around Alvarado Street and downtown Monterey are within roughly a five-to-ten-minute walk. The deluxe king is listed at 310 square feet with a king bed, mini refrigerator, and coffee maker, but no guaranteed view or balcony. The hotel is near the downtown waterfront area, not the Pacific Grove shoreline you were targeting. Reaching Asilomar or the open-coast side of Pacific Grove is a short drive, roughly 10 to 15 minutes depending on traffic.

Its Google score is only 3.9. For this trip only, keep it in the comparison anyway because the savings and dinner access might outweigh that. I’m not changing how we should handle nicer hotel searches after this trip.

Understood. I’ll treat the 3.9 Google rating as a local exception for this Monterey Peninsula decision only. Cypress Cove is currently 4.3 on Google, while Harbor Street is 3.9; those are Google user ratings, not hotel class ratings.

Option three is Ocean Terrace House. Partial-ocean-view king with breakfast for $320 a night. Same tax and assessment. Parking is included. The cancellation wording says free for 48 hours after booking, then the whole stay becomes nonrefundable.

That comes to $1,920 for the room, $230.40 in tax, and the $12 assessment, for a hotel total of $2,162.40. Parking adds nothing, so that is also the complete cost. It stays $87.60 below the hotel limit and costs $33.60 more than Cypress Cove.
Verify what partial ocean view buys us. Is there a balcony, and is breakfast actually included for two?

The named room category guarantees only a partial ocean view; the listing says the water may be visible at an angle and can be partly obstructed. It shows a 285-square-foot room with one king bed, a mini refrigerator, coffee maker, and a small furnished balcony. The rate details include continental breakfast for two registered guests each morning. The current Google user rating is 4.2.
And the cancellation terms on the first two? That third one feels too rigid this far out.

Cypress Cove allows cancellation without penalty through 6:00 p.m. local time on May 13; after that, it charges one night plus tax. Harbor Street allows free cancellation through May 18 at 4:00 p.m.; after the deadline, the first night plus tax is charged. Ocean Terrace is materially stricter: the 48-hour grace period starts when the reservation is made, and after it expires the full six-night amount is nonrefundable.
Put the tradeoff in plain terms. I don’t want the cheapest one automatically winning if it changes the character of the week.

Cypress Cove is the strongest location compromise: $2,128.80 complete, free parking, a genuine walk to the shoreline, and a manageable cancellation deadline, but the smallest room and no promised view. Harbor Street is cheapest at $1,994.40 including parking and has the largest room plus easy dinners, but it shifts the stay into downtown Monterey and requires driving for the open coast. Ocean Terrace provides the only guaranteed water view, balcony, and included breakfast, but costs $2,162.40 and transfers nearly all cancellation risk to you shortly after booking.
How do those numbers change the two retained airport plans? The prior totals used $2,430 for lodging.

Replacing the $2,430 placeholder with Cypress Cove’s $2,128.80 lowers each trip estimate by $301.20. The SJC-arrival/SFO-departure plan would move from $4,134 to $3,832.80. The SFO round trip would move from $4,202 to $3,900.80. Both remain comfortably below the $4,300 airfare, lodging, and rental-car ceiling, and Cypress Cove has no additional parking charge to add.
What would those totals be with Harbor Street, including its parking, and with Ocean Terrace?

Using complete lodging costs, Harbor Street lowers the mixed-airport plan to $3,698.40 and the SFO round trip to $3,766.40. Ocean Terrace puts them at $3,866.40 and $3,934.40, respectively. All three properties fit the overall trip ceiling under either retained airport plan.

Then choose Cypress Cove as the lodging plan. The shoreline walk and cancellation flexibility are worth $134 over Harbor Street, and I don’t want to lock up the entire hotel amount for a partial view. Keep the SFO round trip as the flight backup. Do not book anything yet.

Cypress Cove Inn is now the selected lodging plan for May 20–26, 2028: standard king for six nights, $2,128.80 complete with tax, assessment, and parking. It is about a 0.4-mile walk from public shoreline access, with a smaller 235-square-foot room and no guaranteed ocean view or balcony. Free cancellation runs through 6:00 p.m. local time on May 13. The leading trip combination remains SJC arrival with SFO departure at an estimated $3,832.80, and SFO round trip remains the backup at $3,900.80. Nothing has been booked.
